# PageHeader

The top of a screen: an eyebrow or a back control, trailing actions, and the screen's title in the display face.

## Anatomy

A top row — eyebrow or back on the left, actions on the right — over the title row, which may carry its own trailing slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` *(required)* | `string` | — | — |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | The mono micro-label above the title. Ignored when `back` is given, as in the reference. |
| `back` | `{ label: string; onclick: () => void } \| { label: string; href: string }` | — | Replaces the eyebrow with a back control. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2` | `1` | Heading level. A screen has one h1; a header inside a region takes h2. |
| `id` | `string` | — | — |
| `eyebrowContent` | `Snippet` | — | — |
| `trailing` | `Snippet` | — | — |
| `titleTrailing` | `Snippet` | — | — |

## Variants

Eyebrow, custom eyebrow content, or back. `level` sets whether the title is an `h1` or an `h2`.

## States

Static.

## Keyboard

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Reaches the back control, then the trailing actions. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Activates the back control. |

## ARIA

The title is a real heading. A back control given `href` renders as a link, because going back is navigation.

## Accessibility acceptance criteria

- Reachable, operable and leavable by keyboard alone, with a focus indicator meeting 3:1 in both schemes.
- An accessible name for every control, and current state exposed programmatically.
- No meaning carried by colour alone.
- Legible and operable at a 360px viewport and at desktop width, and at 200% zoom.
- Interactive targets at least 44 × 44px on touch-capable viewports.

## Recorded deviations

| What | Why |
| --- | --- |
| The notification bell is no longer built in. | The reference reaches into a global store from inside the header, which makes the component unusable without that store. The bell goes in the `trailing` slot. |
| A focus indicator was added to the back control. | The reference has none. |
